Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

| sort - click_time

Flyto2 flyto-verification unauthenticated POST /run on :8344 (CVE-2026-67426 SSRF entry) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP POST to the /run endpoint of the flyto-verification service on TCP 8344 from non-loopback/remote sources. The shipped Dockerfile binds 0.0.0.0:8344 and /run has no auth dependency, so any remote POST /run is the unauthenticated entry point for the callback_url SSRF and runner-secret exfiltration chain. Rationale: Uses the article's concrete endpoint (POST /run) and the Dockerfile-shipped port 8344 (verification_service.py:363-364, Dockerfile.verification CMD). Restricting to external/remote sources leverages the fix guidance ('bind loopback by default') to separate attack traffic from legit internal callers. Corroborated against the GitLab advisory confirming the 0.0.0.0:8344 exposure. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/flyto-core/CVE-2026-67426/ • https://cvereports.com/reports/CVE-2026-67426
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate internal verification jobs POSTing /run from an app tier reachable via a public NAT egress IP
  • Vulnerability scanners / ASM tools probing the /run path on 8344
  • Load-balancer or uptime health checks hitting /run
  • Developer testing the verification service from a bastion/VPN with a public source IP
Suppression filter
| where not(SourceIP in ("<known-healthcheck-ip>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the source IP is external and not an expected internal caller; pull the full request (body should contain callback_url/workflowYaml) from app or proxy logs and check whether the host is running flyto-core <= 2.26.6. 2) Contain: rebind flyto-verification to loopback (or firewall 8344 to internal only), and rotate FLYTO_RUNNER_SECRET immediately since it may already be exfiltrated. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2/UC3 — search for outbound connections from the verification host to 169.254.169.254 or to any public IP, and audit engine-callback authentications using the (now-possibly-leaked) runner secret.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort == 8344
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationPort == 8344
| where RequestMethod == "POST"

flyto-verification SSRF to cloud metadata IP (169.254.169.254) — runner-secret/IMDS theft AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts outbound connections from the flyto-verification runner (python/uvicorn/gunicorn/flyto-verification) to cloud instance-metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254, 100.100.100.200, metadata.google.internal). CVE-2026-67426's callback_url bypasses the target_allowed allowlist and SSRF guard, letting an attacker force the service to POST to the IMDS with a controlled body and harvest instance credentials. Rationale: The article explicitly names 'cloud-metadata IP' as an SSRF target; MITRE T1552.005 and Elastic's prebuilt IMDS-SSRF rule confirm 169.254.169.254 (plus Alibaba 100.100.100.200 / GCP metadata.google.internal) as the canonical endpoints. Scoping to the python/flyto-verification process removes legit cloud-agent IMDS calls, making a web-runner->IMDS connection a near-zero-FP signal. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/ • https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/security/prebuilt-rules/rules/cross-platform/credential_access_web_server_cloud_imds_ssrf_request • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pypi/flyto-core/CVE-2026-67426/
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate flyto workflow that intentionally targets an internal 169.254.x host as a callback (rare/misconfig)
  • Cloud SDK embedded in the same python venv making a genuine IMDSv2 token call for the app's own role
  • Security testing / red-team validation of the SSRF fix
  • Sidecar or observability agent sharing the process name 'python' reaching metadata for instance tags
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("flyto", "verification")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is the flyto-verification runner and capture the destination path/body; check IMDS access logs (if IMDSv2 enabled) for a token issuance from this host at the same time. 2) Contain: rotate FLYTO_RUNNER_SECRET and any instance-role credentials that IMDS could have returned; enforce IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=required) and block 169.254.0.0/16 egress from the container; upgrade flyto-core to 2.26.7. 3) Hunt: search CloudTrail/AAD/GCP audit for use of the instance-role or managed-identity credentials from unexpected IPs shortly after this event, and check UC3 for the secret being POSTed to an external attacker host.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254", "100.100.100.200") or RemoteUrl has "metadata.google.internal"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python", "python3", "uvicorn", "gunicorn", "flyto-verification", "flyto")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254", "100.100.100.200") or DstHostname has "metadata.google.internal"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

flyto-verification runner egress to external public host — FLYTO_RUNNER_SECRET exfiltration AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the flyto-verification/python runner initiating outbound connections to public (non-RFC1918, non-link-local) destinations. Because callback_url is attacker-controlled and the service unconditionally attaches X-Internal-Key: $FLYTO_RUNNER_SECRET, any egress from this backend runner to an arbitrary internet host is a candidate secret-exfiltration callback. Rationale: Grounded in the sink from the advisory: post_callback -> session.post(callback_url, headers={'X-Internal-Key': FLYTO_RUNNER_SECRET}) (verification_service.py:330-335). A backend verification runner that is only supposed to call the internal engine should never egress to a public IP, so process-scoped public egress is a high-value exfiltration hunt for the leaked runner secret. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jx74-cqjv-2c67 • https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-67428
ATT&CKT1567 T1552
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate engine callback endpoint hosted on a public IP / SaaS domain rather than internal
  • Python dependency/package fetches (pip, telemetry SDKs) from the same runner venv
  • Outbound calls to a public webhook/notification service used by real workflows
  • CDN or object-storage uploads the workflow performs as designed
Suppression filter
| where RemoteUrl !has "pypi.org" and RemoteUrl !has "pythonhosted.org"
Response runbook
1) Triage: resolve the public RemoteIP/RemoteUrl and compare against the documented internal engine callback host; if it is unknown/attacker-looking, capture the flow and any TLS SNI. 2) Contain: block egress from the flyto-verification container except to the known engine, rotate FLYTO_RUNNER_SECRET, and upgrade to flyto-core 2.26.7. 3) Hunt: correlate with UC1 (inbound POST /run carrying that callback_url) and UC2 (IMDS access), and review engine-callback auth logs for forged authenticated callbacks using the leaked X-Internal-Key.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("flyto-verification", "flyto")) or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python", "python3", "uvicorn", "gunicorn") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "flyto")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess", "ConnectionAttempt")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), Count=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort, 10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
| order by FirstSeen desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.

DeviceNetworkEvents

| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), Count=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort, 10) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
| order by FirstSeen desc
